newsitem.title: GERMANY: Portugal seeks German intervention on Timor issue.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seeks German intervention on Timor issue.

text.p: Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres appealed to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Tuesday to exert a positive influence on Jakarta to improve what he described as "intolerable conditions" in East Timor.

Guterres was speaking in an interview with German radio ahead of a visit by Kohl to Indonesia from October 25 to 29. A German government spokesman said on Monday that Kohl planned to raise human rights issues with government leaders in Jakarta.

"Of course we do not want our friends and allies like Germany to break off relations with Indonesia. On the contrary, we would like these countries to exert a positive influence on Indonesia as far as possible," Guterres told the radio.
"The present situation can not be tolerated for much longer and we are counting on our friends and allies, for example Germany, to help to change things," he said.

Indonesian troops invaded East Timor in December 1975 and Jakarta formally annexed it in July 1976. The United Nations does not recognise Indonesian rule in East Timor and regards former colonial ruler Portugal as the administering power.
Portugal backs the demands of resistance groups that East Timor, which is Roman Catholic while Indonesia is Moslem, should have the right to decide freely on its future.

Guterres said he had personally failed up to now to bring the Indonesian President Suharto into a "constructive dialogue" over granting Timor the right to self-determination during negotiations organised by the United Nations.

"We have completely different positions on this issue. But both sides are prepared to discuss specific ways of improving the dramatic living conditions of these people, who live under military occupation deprived of the most basic rights."

"Indonesia is not changing its policy on these issues," Gueterres said. "This is precisely where the position of an allied country like Germany, an international political heavyweight which is influential in the region, is important".

Guterres echoed the words of Jose Ramos-Horta, an East Timor independence activist, who jointly with East Timor's Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, was last week awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace prize his efforts to establish peace there.
Ramos-Horta told German radio on Monday: "No other country in Europe has the weight, the influence on Indonesia as Germany".
